subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar core support persistent shared-config rules that execute user-selected local commands when quota or provider events occur?
rationale: Implementation review can validate safeguards, but only the repository owner can decide whether this durable local-execution surface belongs in CodexBar's supported product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve after argv repair
options.body: Accept hooks as a supported opt-in core feature after the settings editor preserves argument arrays losslessly and the trust boundary is documented.

options.title: Narrow to config and CLI
options.body: Remove the graphical rule editor for now and expose hooks only through explicit config and CLI workflows, reducing accidental command mutation and casual enablement.

options.title: Decline core execution hooks
options.body: Keep CodexBar observational and leave event-driven command execution to an external watcher or integration.

recommendation.title: Approve after argv repair
recommendation.body: Accept hooks as a supported opt-in core feature after the settings editor preserves argument arrays losslessly and the trust boundary is documented.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, steipete is the best available authority for accepting or rejecting a new persistent local-execution boundary.
